title: Purification of Cafeteria roenbergensis virus particles
author: Matthias Fischer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qz2dx8e

steps.title: Prepare and infect host cultures
steps.instruction: Grow Cafeteria roenbergensis cultures to an initial density of 7E+05 to 1E+06 cells/mL in f/2 artificial seawater medium containing 0.03% (w/v) yeast extract.

substeps.instruction: Dilute denser cultures with f/2-yeast medium if necessary to reach desired concentration.
Aliquot cultures (e.g., 50 ml per 250 ml polycarbonate Erlenmeyer flask or 500 ml per 3 L polycarbonate Fernbach flask).
Infect host cultures with Cafeteria roenbergensis virus (CroV) suspension at a multiplicity of infection (moi) of ~0.01.
Incubate at 20-23 °C (constant shaking not required).
Maintain one uninfected culture as a negative control.

steps.title: Monitor cell density
steps.instruction: Monitor host cell density daily using a hemocytometer until lysis occurs (typically 4-6 days post infection).

steps.title: Remove cell debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysates once cell densities of infected cultures drop below 1E+05 cells/ml to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Use 1 L centrifuge bottles (e.g., Sorvall F9-6x1000 rotor in Sorvall Lynx centrifuges).
Centrifuge at 8000 rcf for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Save the virus-containing supernatant and discard the pellets.

steps.title: Concentrate supernatant via TFF
steps.instruction: Concentrate the CroV-containing supernatant using tangential flow filtration (e.g., Vivaflow 0.2 µm PES unit).

substeps.instruction: Cool the unit and reservoir during concentration.
Check tubing regularly for wear and ensure tight connections.
Maintain back pressure below 2 bars.
Discard filtrate and concentrate the CroV-bacteria mixture to a final volume of 30-50 ml.
Save the concentrate in a 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Perform two-step Optiprep cushion centrifugation
steps.instruction: Use ultracentrifugation on a two-step Optiprep cushion to remove bacteria and further concentrate CroV particles.

substeps.instruction: Fill Beckman SW40 ultraclear tubes with ~6 ml of CroV-bacteria concentrate.
Slowly underlay with 2.5 mL of 23% Optiprep solution (in 50 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl).
Underlay further with 1 mL of 40% Optiprep solution (in 50 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl).
Fill tubes to the top with CroV-bacteria concentrate and balance them.
Centrifuge in a Beckman SW40 swinging bucket rotor (load all buckets) at 100,000 rcf for 2 hours at 15 °C.

steps.title: Collect and dialyze virus particles
steps.instruction: Recover the virus band and remove Optiprep via dialysis.

substeps.instruction: Collect the opaque CroV-containing band at the 23%-40% interface using a 20G needle and syringe (1-2 mL per tube).
Dialyze particles in 3 mL dialysis cassettes (Slide-A-Lyzer, 20 kDa cutoff) against 1 L of 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl at 4°C overnight.

steps.title: Purify via continuous Optiprep gradient
steps.instruction: Perform a second purification using a 10%-50% continuous Optiprep gradient.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10%-50% continuous Optiprep gradients (50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl) in SW40 ultraclear tubes (e.g., Gradient Master: 81.5° angle, 35 rpm, 1 min 15 sec).
Mark tubes at upper half edge and fill with 6.5 mL 10% Optiprep (in 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl).
Load up to 2 mL of dialyzed CroV suspension per tube by replacing the top gradient solution with the suspension.
Centrifuge for 4 h in a SW40 rotor at 100,000 rcf, 4°C.
Extract CroV-containing bands using a 21G needle and syringe.

steps.title: Final pelleting and resuspension
steps.instruction: Remove remaining Optiprep and concentrate the virus into a final pellet.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the CroV-Optiprep suspension 3-fold with 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl.
Spin in a tabletop centrifuge for 20 min at 4°C and 10,000 rcf (use lower g-forces/longer times if intact particles are required).
Save the supernatant.
Dissolve opaque pellets in 50 µl of 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 2 mM MgCl2, 400 mM NaCl.
Combine dissolved pellets and spin again for 15 min at 8,000 g, 4°C to form a white pellet.
Carefully resuspend the virus pellet.
Optional: Centrifuge saved supernatants for 1 h at maximum speed (20,000 rcf), 4°C to collect remaining particles for DNA extraction.
